name: Juan de Mena
bio: Juan de Mena (1411–1456) was born in Córdoba, studied at Salamanca and spent time in Rome, and became Latin secretary and chronicler to King Juan II of Castile. He was a learned court poet in the circle of the Marqués de Santillana and the royal favourite Álvaro de Luna.

His Laberinto de Fortuna (1444), also called Las trescientas after its roughly three hundred stanzas of arte mayor, is an allegorical vision in the manner of Dante: led by Providence, the poet sees the wheels of Fortune and the circles of the planets peopled with figures of history and of his own time. Its Latinate diction and syntax made it the most admired and most annotated Castilian poem of the fifteenth century.

poems.title: Canción: Donde yago en esta cama
poems.author: Juan de Mena
poems.collection: The Oxford Book of Spanish Verse (1913)
poems.text:
Donde yago enesta cama,
la mayor pena de mi
es pensar quando parti
de entre braços de mi dama.

A bueltas del mal que siento
de mi partida, pardios,
tantas vezes me arrepiento
quantas me miembro de vos:
tanto que me hazen fama
que de aquesto adoleci,
los que saben que parti
de entre braços de mi dama.

Aunque padezco y me callo,
por esto mis tristes quexos,
no menos cerca los hallo
que vuestros bienes de lexos;
si la fin es que me llama,
o que muerte que perdi,
en biuir quando parti
de entre braços de mi dama.
